https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/a.text: 1:12 Typhoon Dolphin batters parts of east and south-east Asia – video Extreme weather Typhoon Dolphin: more than a million people evacuated in China as record rainfall dumped on Shanghai Authorities warn that days of intense rain could trigger widespread flooding and landslides as storm moves north and further inland Yu-chen Li in Taipei Mon 10 Aug 2026 00.55 EDT First published on Sun 9 Aug 2026 23.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google More than a million people were moved to safety across eastern China by Sunday evening as powerful Typhoon Dolphin made landfall amid fears torrential rain would cause flooding and landslides. Wenzhou, a coastal city in Zhejiang province, said it relocated more than 900,000 people and opened more than 1,500 emergency shelters. In neighbouring Fujian, 98,900 people were moved from high-risk areas. Hong Kong records hottest day ever as Typhoon Dolphin fuels heatwave Read more In Shanghai, 215,600 people were moved from areas considered at risk by Sunday evening, substantially higher than an earlier figure of 30,300. A weather station in central Shanghai recorded nearly 313mm of rain in the 24 hours to 7am on Monday, its highest 24-hour rainfall in more than 150 years of records. Another station in the city recorded nearly 400mm. The hashtag “Shanghai turns into the sea” began trending on the Chinese social media platform Weibo, as videos circulated showing streets flooded around the Wukang Mansion, one of the city’s best-known tourist landmarks. The average rainfall recorded across Zhejiang from Friday evening to Monday morning reached 173mm, reportedly surpassing the levels seen during previous major typhoons including Lekima and Bavi. Dolphin weakened rapidly to a tropical storm by 5am on Monday. But as the storm continued to move northwards and farther inland, heavy rain was forecast across large parts of eastern and central China , extending north into Shandong and affecting Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Shanghai. Authorities maintained an orange alert for heavy rain and warned that days of intense rain could trigger widespread flooding and landslides through Wednesday, urging people to stay indoors during the heavy downpours. Forecasters in China predicted some areas could see 200-400mm (7.9–15.7 inches) of rainfall over the coming days. View image in fullscreen A temporary shelter in Hangzhou, where thousands of people were evacuated because of Typhoon Dolphin. Photograph: VCG/Getty Images The storm forced Shanghai’s two airports to cancel more than 1,300 flights. Public transport services, including many local trains, have been suspended in the financial hub. Zhejiang’s Ningbo international airport, about 150km south of Shanghai, will resume flight operations from midday (0400 GMT) on Monday. But the airport warned some journeys may yet be delayed or cancelled. Provincial capital Hangzhou resumed subway services on Monday morning, after halting some train operations on Sunday. Elsewhere, Dolphin fuelled intense heat over Hong Kong on Sunday, pushing the city to its highest ever temperature of 36.9C . The extremely hot weather was expected to continue into Tuesday, officials said. In Taiwan, ferry services were suspended and more than 180 flights were cancelled as the storm brought downpours and strong winds on Sunday. Dolphin earlier swept through Japan’s southern Okinawa prefecture, injuring six people and ⁠cutting power to more than 50,000 buildings. In the Philippines, the typhoon did not make landfall in the country’s north but intensified the seasonal monsoon rains, which flooded many areas of the main northern Luzon region, including around Manila. Scientists say global warming has made extreme weather more likely, including more powerful typhoons. (Photo by Ronny HARTMANN / AFP) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip European officials stated there is no evidence that Russia is preparing for a conventional military attack on NATO or the Baltic states, pushing back against reports regarding the primary focus of CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s recent unannounced visit to Moscow . According to Bloomberg , Ratcliffe’s visit likely addressed efforts to end the war in Ukraine, reaffirmed NATO’s Article 5 mutual defense commitments, and covered the ongoing conflict with Iran. Sources indicated that Ratcliffe may have also sought to deter Russian retaliation against US economic measures targeting Iran and to press Moscow to cease its support for Tehran. European officials noted they had not received a formal US briefing on the trip, basing their assessments on independent intelligence and historical US operating procedures. Advertisement While noting that maintaining intelligence channels with Russia is routine, sources told Bloomberg it was notable that Ratcliffe appeared to want the visit made public. The officials acknowledged a rise in Russian hybrid operations, including assassination attempts, sabotage, and airspace incursions, noting that Europe has largely been unprepared for the incidents. However, they stressed that recent intelligence shows no shift in Russia’s conventional military posture that would indicate an impending attack. To mitigate the risk of miscalculation amid the growing hybrid threats, NATO allies have reportedly been discussing how to enhance intelligence and military engagement with Russia. Other Topics of Interest Polish PM Tusk Warns of Russian Escalation in Coming Months Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated that Russia is actively preparing for an escalation of tension during the upcoming autumn and winter. Tusk warns of regional escalation The European officials’ assessments contrast with recent warnings from Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who stated on Friday, Aug. 28, that Russia is actively preparing for further escalation. Speaking in Olsztyn, Tusk described the upcoming autumn and winter as critical for the security of Ukraine , Poland, and the wider region. Addressing Ratcliffe’s Moscow trip, Tusk noted that Warsaw was not surprised due to its constant coordination with the CIA, though he emphasized that the current security situation extends well beyond the scope of the intelligence director’s visit. Advertisement Tusk’s stark security warning comes days after Polish and Ukrainian leaders exchanged public messages reaffirming their bilateral ties amid the ongoing war. Ukrainian officials confirmed the receipt of an Independence Day letter from Polish President Karol Nawrocki to President Volodymyr Zelensky, in which Nawrocki wished Ukraine victory in its existential struggle against Russia and the full restoration of its internationally recognized borders.
